frase_gancho.texto: A warrior goddess of clay who gave her life in childbirth.

puente_narrativo.texto: We remain in central Veracruz with another clay figure, this time a female one, linked to the women who died in childbirth.

guion_corto.texto: Cihuateteo is a Nahuatl word. It refers to women who died giving birth, who were revered as warriors. This sculpture comes from El Zapotal, in Veracruz, and dates to the Late Classic, between 600 and 900 AD. It is modeled in clay, which means it is ceramic. There is a detail about dates that helps in looking at it. The best-known tradition about the cihuateteo is that of the Mexica, who lived much later, between 1250 and 1521. A related piece exists at Calixtlahuaca, and that one is indeed Mexica. Thus, a clay figure from the coast shares a name with a tradition of the Highlands.

guion_largo.texto:
Cihuateteo is the plural of cihuateotl, a Nahuatl word meaning woman goddess. The name is applied to women who died during childbirth. Among the Mexica they were revered as heroic warriors, who had given their lives in what they called the battle of birth.

According to that tradition, they lived in the region of the west and accompanied the Sun from midday until it set on the horizon. Their myth gave rise, in colonial times, to the legend of La Llorona.

The sculpture in this hall comes from El Zapotal, in Veracruz, and is modeled in clay. It belongs to the Late Classic, between 600 and 900 AD. That is several centuries before the Mexica, who lived between 1250 and 1521. For that reason, the Mexica tradition helps us understand the name. But it cannot be taken for granted that it explains everything this figure meant to those who made it.

A related piece exists at Calixtlahuaca, in the Highlands, and that one is indeed Mexica. Comparing them shows that the idea of honoring women who died in childbirth appears in different places and times.

Look at the figure slowly. It is a female image modeled in clay. Ask yourself what its posture and its face tell you.

texto: Notice that it is modeled in clay, not carved in stone.
Take your time looking at the details of the face and the body.
Compare this figure with the Mexica tradition of the cihuateteo, which came later.

texto.pregunta: Myth: The cihuateteo were witches or demons of the night.
texto.respuesta: Reality: The word refers to women who died giving birth, who were revered as warriors.
